classification.difficultyReason: Justify the diagram angles and combine the supplied sine-rule and right-triangle expressions.

content.prompt:
Two towers $AB$ and $PQ$ stand on level ground. The angles of elevation of the top of the taller tower from the top and bottom of the shorter tower are $5°$ and $20°$ respectively.
The height of the taller tower is 70 metres.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 14 tower diagram beneath part d
spec.description: Schematic towers AB and PQ, horizontal ground BQ, horizontal AK, diagonal BP crossing AK at J, and AP joining the tops. Preserve the external 5° curved leader, internal 20° label and external vertical double-headed 70 m dimension.
spec.mathematics: AB and PQ vertical; BQ and AK horizontal; J lies on BP and AK. Elevations are 5° at A and 20° at B. PQ=70 m. Drawn slopes follow the schematic source rather than numerical angle scale.

answer.worked: $AK\parallel BQ$, so $\angle PJK=20°$. The exterior angle of $\triangle APJ$ gives $\angle APJ=20°-5°=15°$.

$\angle BAP=90°+5°=95°$. By the sine rule in $\triangle ABP$,
$$\begin{align*}\frac{AB}{\sin15°}&=\frac{BP}{\sin95°}\\[8pt]AB&=\frac{BP\sin15°}{\sin95°}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: Hence find the height of the shorter tower, correct to the nearest metre.
